title: Do while statements
recap: A do while loop checks its condition after the body, so the body always runs at least once. The semicolon after the condition is required.
Use a do while when the work must happen once before the decision, such as printing a countdown that includes its starting value even when the start is zero.
objectives: Implement digitCount from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement digitCount with a do while loop. Return the number of decimal digits in a nonnegative integer. Zero has one digit, which is why the loop must run at least once. Return -1 for negative inputs. Repeated integer division by 10 removes the last digit; do not convert the number to text.
hints: Reject negative values before the loop.
Increase the count once, then divide the value by 10.
Repeat while the remaining value is greater than zero.
